tier_reason: Public benchmark code in the repo (benchmark/pbtools/main.c, benchmark/google/main.cpp, benchmark/protobuf-c/main.c with their Makefiles and benchmark/common.mk), gcc 8.3.0, per-row optimization flags and the CPU (Intel Core i7-4510U @ 2.00GHz) are all stated in benchmark/README.rst, and the rows compare directly against Google protobuf C++ and protobuf-c. The -O3 baseline flags are also in public git history (common.mk had OPT_SPEED = -O3 until commit 6000b5f).

corrections.claimed_speedup: Encoding (Message plus Message3, 2,000,000 iterations each): pbtools -O2 1.457 s vs Google protobuf C++ -O3 2.231 s (about 1.53x, derived from page data) and vs protobuf-c -O3 1.892 s (about 1.30x, derived from page data). Decoding: pbtools -O2 1.594 s vs Google -O3 1.997 s (about 1.25x, derived from page data) and vs protobuf-c -O3 2.508 s (about 1.57x, derived from page data). With -O2 -flto pbtools encodes in 1.319 s and decodes in 1.239 s. At -Os pbtools encodes in 3.398 s, slower than protobuf-c -Os (1.970 s) but faster than Google -Os (3.713 s); at -Os pbtools decodes in 1.749 s vs Google 2.350 s and protobuf-c 2.609 s. An earlier run (September 2019, all at -O3, replaced in commit 6000b5f) had pbtools at 1.118 s encode and 1.069 s decode.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: gcc/g++ 8.3.0 with -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections -Wl,--gc-sections (benchmark/common.mk); per-row flags in the README tables: pbtools -O2, -O2 -flto, -Os, -Os -flto; protobuf-c -O3, -O3 -flto, -Os, -Os -flto (libprotobuf-c linked statically); Google -O3 and -Os (generated code and main only, linked against a shared libprotobuf 3.6.1 whose own build flags are not stated). The -O3 rows come from the September 2019 run when common.mk had OPT_SPEED = -O3; commit 6000b5f (2020-01-16) switched OPT_SPEED to -O2 and re-ran only pbtools, nanopb and flatbuffers.
corrections.workload: Encode and decode of two protobuf messages from a proto derived from Google's protobuf benchmark messages (benchmark/benchmark.proto, java_package com.google.protobuf.benchmarks): 'Message' wrapping Message1 with a 566-byte wire size and Message3 with a 106-byte wire size, 2,000,000 iterations each, per library; whole-process time per row.
corrections.caveats: Benchmark is first-party, single run per row, no variance reported, small messages only, and the toolchain is old (gcc 8.3.0, Google libprotobuf/libprotoc 3.6.1 as a distro shared library, protobuf-c version not stated). The headline mixes two runs: the Google and protobuf-c -O3 rows date from September 2019 (common.mk then had OPT_SPEED = -O3), while the pbtools -O2 rows come from a January 2020 re-run (commit 6000b5f switched to -O2 and the top-level benchmark Makefile only rebuilds nanopb and pbtools), so the baselines were not re-measured against the pbtools version shown; the current Makefiles would build every library at -O2. Harness differences favour pbtools: its encode loop fills a fixed stack workspace and stores pointers to string literals, Google's encode loop constructs a fresh heap-allocated benchmark::Message every iteration (no Arena, although the proto sets cc_enable_arenas) and copies both ~230-byte strings before SerializeToString into a std::string, and protobuf-c encodes through pack_to_buffer with a ProtobufCBufferSimple callback rather than its direct pack() call (stack structs, no malloc on encode). On decode protobuf-c mallocs and frees the whole message tree per iteration (unpack with the default allocator), Google reuses one message object, and pbtools copies strings into its arena workspace. At -Os pbtools encoding is slower than protobuf-c (3.398 s vs 1.970 s). FlatBuffers decodes in 0.100 s (-O2) only because it decodes lazily. The repo's guessed baseline (msgpack) is wrong: msgpack is not in the benchmark. No commits since 2023-06-04.

notes: All headline numbers match benchmark/README.rst exactly and the derived ratios check out. Shortcomings to record: baseline rows (Google, protobuf-c at -O3) are from a September 2019 run not repeated when pbtools was re-measured at -O2 in January 2020; Google's encode loop builds a fresh heap message per iteration without an Arena and protobuf-c uses the slower pack_to_buffer path; first-party single run on gcc 8.3.0 and protobuf 3.6.1; pbtools loses to protobuf-c on -Os encoding; abandoned since 2023-06-04 (MIT, 82 stars, not a fork, not archived).
